name: APT41
affiliation_detail:
In September 2020, the DOJ unsealed charges against five Chinese nationals and two Malaysian accomplices in connection with APT41's operations. Three defendants were employees of the front company Chengdu 404 Network Technology (成都肆零肆网络科技有限公司), a purported network security firm based in Chengdu, Sichuan Province. Intercepted communications revealed one defendant boasting of close relationships with both the MSS and MPS. The indictments covered attacks against over 100 organizations worldwide, including supply chain compromises, ransomware attacks (including against a non-profit combating global poverty), and theft of source code, digital certificates, and customer data.
The two Malaysian nationals were arrested in Malaysia in September 2020 for conspiring with APT41 members to profit from video game company intrusions. All five Chinese defendants remain at large.
description:
APT41 is a Chinese state-sponsored threat group characterized by conducting state-directed cyber espionage aligned with China's strategic intelligence requirements while simultaneously engaging in cybercrime activities. (FireEye, 2019) Active since at least 2012, APT41 has targeted organizations in at least 14 countries across large number of industries. According to U.S. DOJ, APT41 operated through the front company Chengdu 404 Network Technology and was reportedly connected to both MSS and MPS.
APT41 is known for its usage of software supply chain attacks, compromising software development environments and injecting malicious code into trusted update mechanisms. FireEye (2019) attributes the 2017 NetSarang ShadowPad compromise, and the 2019 ASUS Live Update utility (ShadowHammer) to APT41. The 2017 CCleaner compromise, while overlapping with APT41 TTPs, is not definitely attributed to the group by FireEye.
SentinelOne's 2021 research identified APT41 as comprising two sub-groups: BARIUM, responsible for the major supply chain attacks (NetSarang, ASUS ShadowHammer and allegedlly CCleaner); and LEAD, conducting broader espionage and financial operations. Both sub-groups are, according to the authors, based in Chengdu.
In February 2026 Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) observed APT41 misusing Google Gemini AI to accelerate  the development and deployment of malicious tooling, including for knowledge synthesis, real-time troubleshooting, and code translation."

campaigns.name: Video Game Industry Targeting and Virtual Currency Theft
campaigns.description: APT41's financially motivated campaign, targeting video game development studios, distributors, and publishers. The group manipulated virtual currencies, stole in-game resources for real-world sale, and stole source code and digital certificates.

sources.title: APT41, A DUAL ESPIONAGE AND CYBER CRIME OPERATION

campaigns.name: Supply Chain Attacks (NetSarang, ASUS)
campaigns.description: APT41's most technically sophisticated campaigns, compromising software vendor build environments to distribute backdoored updates. The 2017 CCleaner attack distributed trojanized software to approximately 2.2 million users, with ShadowPad deployed selectively using MAC address filtering against approximately 11 technology companies. The 2017 NetSarang attack injected ShadowPad into the Xmanager and Xshell server management tools. The 2019 ASUS ShadowHammer attack distributed backdoored ASUS Live Update signed with legitimate certificates, targeting approximately 600 specific MAC addresses. All three attacks demonstrated surgical precision within mass distribution.

campaigns.name: Mass Exploitation Campaign (Citrix/Cisco/Zoho)
campaigns.description: Between January and March 2020, APT41 launched a sweeping campaign exploiting recently disclosed vulnerabilities in Citrix ADC (CVE-2019-19781), Cisco RV320 routers, and Zoho ManageEngine Desktop Central (CVE-2020-10189). FireEye described it as one of the most widespread campaigns from a China-nexus espionage actor in recent years, targeting at least 75 organizations across banking, defense, government, healthcare, high-tech, manufacturing, oil and gas, pharmaceuticals, telecommunications, and transportation in over 20 countries.

campaigns.name: U.S. State Government Targeting
campaigns.description: Mandiant documented a sustained campaign targeting U.S. state government networks. APT41 exploited vulnerabilities in internet-facing web applications, including a zero-day in a commercial animal health management application, and deployed the DEADEYE dropper with LOWKEY backdoor.

sources.title: Does This Look Infected? APT41 Targeting U.S. State Governments

campaigns.name: Global Espionage Campaigns (Group-IB 2021)
campaigns.description: Group-IB documented four distinct APT41 campaigns in 2021, resulting in approximately 80 proactive notifications to affected organizations worldwide. The campaigns used Cobalt Strike infrastructure for C2 and targeted government and private sector entities. Work schedule analysis confirmed operators working 9 AM to 7 PM in the UTC+8 time zone (consistent with Chengdu).

sources.title: 4 Malicious Campaigns and a New Wave of APT41 Attacks
